prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live web access, so I can’t pull current local business listings or verify recent reviews. I can, however, help you find a reliable contractor in Joplin, MO and give practical tools to vet and choose one. If you want, I can also draft messages and a bid-comparison sheet you can use when contacting contractors.

Where to look (quick places to start)
- Google Maps and Yelp — look for contractors with many recent positive reviews and photos of completed work.  
- Angi (formerly Angie’s List), HomeAdvisor, Houzz, Thumbtack — filtered by project type and area.  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) — check ratings and complaints.  
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce — local members and referrals.  
- Facebook neighborhood groups / Nextdoor — neighbor recommendations and before/after photos.  
- Local supply stores (Ace, local lumber yards, Home Depot Pro Desk) — staff often know reputable contractors.  
- Ask friends/neighbors who had similar work done — a personal referral is often best.

Local checks and records
- Jasper County or City of Joplin building department — see if the contractor has a history of pulling permits for work and whether any complaints or code issues exist.  
- For trades like electricians, plumbers, and HVAC, check state/local licensing/registration and verify the license number with the appropriate regulator.

How to vet contractors (step-by-step)
1. Get at least 3 written bids for the same scope of work.  
2. Ask for references for similar projects (ideally local). Call and ask about timeliness, workmanship, and communication.  
3. Verify insurance: general liability and workers’ comp (ask for certificates).  
4. Confirm licensing for any required trades (electrical, plumbing, HVAC). Missouri does not require a statewide general contractor license, so licensing matters most for specialty trades.  
5. Check BBB and online reviews; look for patterns, not single bad reviews.  
6. Ask who will do the work — the named contractor or subcontractors — and get their names and qualifications.  
7. Require a written contract with schedule, payment terms, change-order process, and clean-up responsibilities.  
8. Ask about warranties for labor and manufacturer warranties for materials.  
9. Avoid large upfront payments (common schedule: deposit, progress payments, final payment upon completion and lien releases).  
10. Ask about permits — reputable contractors will pull them and submit to inspections.

Red flags
- No written contract or unwillingness to detail scope and timeline.  
- Asks for full payment up front.  
- No local references or recent portfolio photos.  
- Poor or nonexistent insurance proof.  
- Vague answers about who will perform the work or about permits.

Questions to ask a contractor (sample)
- How long have you been doing this type of project in Joplin?  
- Can you provide 3 local references and photos of completed work?  
- Are you insured (general liability and workers’ comp)? Can you provide certificates?  
- Will you pull permits? Who is responsible for inspections?  
- What is the projected start date and completion timeline?  
- What is the payment schedule and what is included in the price?  
- Do you provide a written warranty? If so, for how long and what is covered?  
- Who will be on-site each day? Will you use subcontractors?

If you want help next
- Tell me the type of project (bathroom, kitchen, whole-house remodel, roof, siding, deck, etc.), approximate budget, and when you want it done. I can:  
  - Draft an outreach email/message you can send to contractors.  
  - Create a comparison checklist/spreadsheet to evaluate bids.  
  - Provide a sample contract checklist or change-order form.

If you’d like, give me the project details and I’ll prepare the outreach template and vetting checklist tailored to your job.
